market_holds: No usable option chain (baseline: empty_chain), so the usual move is the 7-print median historical reaction, 9.89% (max 20.45%, 3 of 7 up). Spot 18.84 at the 13:08 ET seal. Consensus (Yahoo earningsTrend, read 2026-11-17, 5 analysts): FQ4 revenue $54.49M (-0.75% y/y) and adj EPS $0.262; FY26 $217.74M / $1.072; FY27 $228.40M (+4.9%) / $1.218. Estimates were essentially flat for 90 days (FQ4 EPS 0.265 -> 0.262). Against the August guide (FY26 revenue $216-221M, adj EBITDA $57-60M, adj EPS $1.08-1.12) less nine-month actuals ($163.256M revenue, $43.516M adj EBITDA, $0.82 adj EPS) the implied FQ4 is $52.7-57.7M revenue (mid $55.2M), $13.5-16.5M EBITDA, $0.26-0.30 EPS, so consensus sits in the lower part of the revenue range and at the very bottom of the EPS range. FY27 consensus +4.9% equals management's August 'mid-single digits' framing (cut from high-single), with 100-200bp margin expansion framed. Sentiment reset in August: Benchmark and StoneX to Hold, KeyBanc PT $27->$20, DA Davidson $30->$28; Stephens initiated Hold $23 on 2026-11-13. Short interest 2.85M shares at 2026-10-30 (prior month 3.32M), about 16% of 18.0M Class A shares, short ratio 8.35 days. Run-in: from the 2026-09-30 low close of $13.82 to $18.76 (+35.7%), alongside gov-tech peer TYL +30.9% over the same span, while IGV fell 9.6% and IWM 3.0%; last 5 sessions -2.5%; still below the $21.96 pre-August close. The line it trades on: the guide. Three successive guide reductions (initial FY26 guide below consensus Nov 2025 -10.5%, midpoint lowered May 2026 -7.7%, cut Aug 2026 -20.5%).
view: This print is two things: an FQ4 that has to land inside an already-cut FY26 guide, and the first formal FY27 guide. The FQ4 bar is low: consensus revenue $54.5M and EPS $0.262 sit at or below the bottom half of the guide-implied quarter, and management cut in August with knowledge of the utilities CIS delay, so a quarter at or modestly above consensus is the more likely outcome (recurring revenue ~80% of mix and growing ~8%; non-recurring down ~18% in FQ3 and flagged to keep declining y/y in FQ4; at those rates FQ4 lands around $55M). But the stock trades on the guide, and FY27 consensus ($228.4M, +4.9%; EPS $1.22) already equals management's own August 'mid-single digits plus 100-200bp margin' framing, so an in-line guide is roughly priced. The organic arithmetic behind that framing is fragile (FQ3 organic revenue -2% per call coverage; recurring +8% partly acquired; professional services still falling), and this management has drifted its guide down three times in a row and set last year's initial guide below consensus with a wide range. Against that: positioning (16% of Class A short, ~8 days to cover, covering under way in October) means an in-line guide plus an FQ4 beat could squeeze, and the stock is cheap relative to TYL. The +36% run off the September low came with the gov-tech peer re-rating (TYL +31%) and short covering, not with i3 news, so it raises the bar modestly without telling me how the guide lands. Net: a slight lean down on guide-credibility history, offset by a low quarterly bar and a short base; not enough for a call.

recommendation.reason: The deciding line is the FY27 guide versus a consensus ($228.4M, +4.9%) that already matches management's own August framing; I found no dated evidence since August (customer, counterparty, contract or executive remark) that moves the guide's likely midpoint either side of that number. The FQ4 bar is low and the short base is large, which cuts against the guide-drift history, so neither side reaches 65.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: An FY27 revenue guide with a midpoint at or above ~$230M and margin expansion at the top of 100-200bp (would make me lean up, squeeze-sized), or a midpoint near $224M or below with professional-services weakness extended into FY27 (lean down, ~10%+).

self_critique: The case for up is real: a quarterly bar set at the bottom of the guide, a management that cut in August precisely to have something beatable, an FY27 consensus that merely matches their own framing, and 16% of Class A shares short at ~8 days to cover after a month of covering; an in-line guide could easily produce a +8-12% squeeze at the open. The case for down is the three-in-a-row guide drift, negative organic growth and continuing professional-services weakness. I cannot separate these with dated evidence, so the honest answer is near 50.
